feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It is clear and polished overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” which boosts credibility.  
- Broad but coherent skill set across strategy, platforms, analytics, content operations, and production, well aligned to public-sector digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Summary, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate overlapping sections to improve scannability and avoid keyword overloading.  
- Tighten bullet writing for impact: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Add more measurable results where possible (engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings).  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should drop the comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization wide” should be standardized; title casing is inconsistent (“AI Hybrid Search,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT”). No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and add scale where possible to increase impact.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “driving.”
- Consider this rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads Drupal-based platform transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and audience engagement.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled” consistently throughout or vary only with purpose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector communications,” “governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” are already echoed in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.
- “Multimedia production” is also repeated in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Prioritize strategic, senior-level capabilities over operational phrasing; e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Tighten and standardize terms for parallel structure: “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure,” “Workflow automation and platform integration.”
- Consider a sharper version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Use “and” instead of “&” for consistency with the rest of the CV’s more formal style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it shorter or more distinct.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps directly with both Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from role bullets.
- Tighten wording and standardize style: use parallel verb-led phrasing and consistent lists without overstacking nouns.
- Add 1 concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail where possible (for example, users, content volume, campaign reach, or event context).
- Revise for concision: “bill-level AI chat” is clear, but “structured content workflows” and “modular structure designed for continued campaign growth” could be simplified.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo role bullets; consider making this a “Selected Projects” block with more specific deliverables or outcomes.
- Anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator because it adds cross-channel and experiential work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consulting impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Streamlined cross-channel workflows,” “launched modular campaign experiences,” “improved governance/usability.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Lead enterprise web and content-operations improvements, refining workflows, governance, and analytics for coordinated communications.
- Build Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Provide front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for public-facing web properties.
- Shape an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success, or toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consultant scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel and analytics bullets more results-oriented: add growth, engagement, efficiency, reporting adoption, or decision-making impact if available.
- Tighten wording: replace “including”/“along with” phrasing; use action + outcome structure in each bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video leadership may overlap with older NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio as a new organizational capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows clear advancement without repeating team/platform leadership language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale/outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution and, if possible, metrics: “Built editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved cross-team coordination, content consistency and delivery speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director role’s channel oversight; use “managed execution” instead of “led.”
- Weekly video/livestream language risks repeating the 2015–2018 role unless you clarify this role scaled or formalized the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for a more senior phrase like “content operations” or “content strategy” to better match director/consultant-level work.
- If space allows, align wording more closely to recent impact areas, e.g. “enterprise web governance” or “digital communications systems,” which better reflect 2022–present experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” closely duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too broad and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline skills line, tighten it to the most marketable, recent capabilities and group related tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a raw tool list to a sharper capability-led line:
  Web platforms & technical execution: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Put Drupal first and keep Power Pages only if relevant to target roles; it’s less supported by recent experience than Drupal/CMS modernization.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If possible, add one proof point elsewhere rather than here, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ pages” in experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Most tools repeat the Technical + IT section; this topline item should stay selective, not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics leadership rather than just listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Use grouped, cleaner wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic items with stronger business language: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool elsewhere; let this section signal senior capability, and keep the full stack in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent in-house studio/event leadership rather than basic task lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and delivery level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrasing like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Live and hybrid event production” to avoid sounding dated and broaden applicability.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “supporting advocacy programming and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to be more specific, not repetitive.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ may be better kept only if targeting multimedia-heavy roles; otherwise it can feel narrower than the rest of the CV.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize level of use and recency.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, group by strength: **Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Put Drupal first and add a qualifier tied to recent impact, since it is clearly the dominant platform in recent roles.
- Consider removing GitHub Pages if it was only lightly used; it is less aligned with the enterprise/public-sector positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version more strategic and this one more tool-specific.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so avoid repeating that phrase here unless you add platform-specific context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- Group related items for readability: front-end (HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery), integration (APIs, GTM), deployment/automation (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions).
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context in another section, e.g., “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment automation for Drupal-based public web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions; keep this item focused on technical tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as an undifferentiated software list. Since workflow automation is already a core competency, this item should emphasize systems-building tools over generic collaboration apps and align with recent enterprise workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to highlight automation first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration tools out unless they were admin/implementation responsibilities; **Slack, Teams, Basecamp, Trello** weaken the section because they’re common workplace tools.
- If accurate, add scope via wording in the title or grouping: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems** or split into **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Work Management:** Jira, Asana
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes rather than listing more tools, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate to streamline publishing and reporting operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis without adding specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; keep only the strongest/current tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic tools dump. Since recent roles emphasize leading email/newsletter operations, this item should signal level of ownership and enterprise relevance, not just product names.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (journey automation)** • **Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**
- If space allows, tie to outcomes rather than tools elsewhere in experience bullets, e.g., newsletter scale, segmentation, automation, or engagement improvement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience; keep this section tool-focused and leave audience scale/results to recent roles.
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless supported by CRM/automation language; consider “Email Marketing & Journey Automation” instead.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capability, not just software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Reorder for impact: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a more specific term like **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards**
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability instead of another generic term: **tagging strategy**, **conversion tracking**, or **behavior analysis**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two or making this version more tool-specific.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this line with the same exact framing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-career buildout work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates; coordinated day-to-day publishing across channels.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later, more senior roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation support plus the podcast as a concrete first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and digital content development; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “coordinated innovation and research projects” and “contributed to digital content production” with clearer scope: research support, program communications, multimedia asset creation.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or types of stakeholders/programs supported.
- Keep it to one concise sentence or two short bullets; this is an older role, so avoid overbuilding it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/program support.
- Avoid repeating leadership language better reserved for 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.

Suggested edit:
